title: I Tried the Accelerated Dragon... Not What I Expected

facts.fact: The video shows three online games in which the streamer plays Black and tries the Accelerated Dragon (Sicilian with an early ...g6).
facts.trap: The video is a single game.
facts.note: Games start at 0:00, 17:12 and 36:38. Streamer is likely Alex Banzea (caption spells the email 'alexpansza.com').

evidence.quote: Welcome back to another game with the black pieces. Uh, we're going to be trying to play the accelerated dragon.

facts.fact: In the first game the opponent avoided sharp lines, the game turned into a technical endgame rather than aggressive play, and the streamer won it, largely thanks to an active king.
facts.trap: The first game was a sharp attacking Dragon game.

evidence.quote: We ended up playing technical chess, so not so much uh aggressive stuff as expected

facts.fact: In the second game the opponent played an unambitious c3; the streamer got a big advantage but threw it away with one rushed move (should have played ...e5), reached an equal endgame, and still won after the opponent made mistakes and his pawns promoted.

evidence.quote: messed up big advantage, but okay

facts.fact: In the third game the opponent chose the Alapin (2.c3); the streamer answered with ...d5 into an isolated-queen's-pawn structure, still fianchettoing as in the Accelerated Dragon, aiming to trade pieces toward a safe, slightly better endgame.

evidence.quote: against Alapin, we're going to be going for pawn to D5, going for isolated pawn uh structures

facts.fact: The third (final) game ended in a draw even though the streamer was dominating; he admits he missed a win (a knight f4 double attack).
facts.trap: The streamer won the final game (or won all three games).
facts.note: Missed win noted at 42:57: 'I think I had missed win'.

evidence.quote: Only only made a draw, but I was dominating um this game.
